chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the milk of camels, sheep, and cattle, and their urine and meat. He said: “Do not perform wudu (ablution) because of it; and if something from it reaches you, or your garment, then do not wash it, unless you wish to clean yourself.”

He said: And I asked him about the urine of riding animals, mules, and donkeys. He said: “Wash it; and if you do not know its place, then wash the whole garment; and if you are in doubt, then sprinkle water over it.”

key_terms.أَلْبَانِ: the milk of the mentioned animals
key_terms.لَا تَوَضَّأْ: do not perform wudu (ablution) on account of it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on animal urine on clothing according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings on the taharah and najasah of substances from different animals. It states that the milk, urine, and meat-related contact of camels, sheep, and cattle do not require washing, while the urine of riding animals, mules, and donkeys is to be washed from the garment, with further instruction when the exact place is unknown or doubtful.
